properties.description:
`incomplete_published_contract` — an Interface designated `published` or `both` with any of the nine structured agreement axes unanswered. Per-contract, severity 0.45: below `unverified_published_contract` (0.6), because a published promise with NO evidence at all is a stronger finding than one whose description has gaps; above the ordinary 0.3 notes, because an undescribed seam is what makes two designs uncheckable against each other.

SERVES `req:interface-spec-complete`, accepted and unimplemented until now. Its point is not completeness for its own sake — two designs cannot be checked for INCOMPATIBILITY at a seam unless the seam is described in comparable terms, so `mirror_surface` could link two designs and still not tell you they disagree.

⭐ THE ONE THAT NEARLY GOT AWAY: `unspecified` IS UNSET. Five of the nine axes are enums DEFAULTING to `unspecified`, and the store materialises defaults on write — so a presence test counts the word as an answer, and the first cut of this detector was GREEN OVER EXACTLY WHAT IT EXISTS TO CHECK. Measured before the fix: `ifc:mcp-tools-http` read 9 of 9 complete while its `medium` said `unspecified`, and `ifc:graph-export` reported 4 gaps where there are 6. Recorded in full as `fact:a-materialised-default-defeats-a-completeness-check` — read before this node was created and judged DISTINCT: that fact is the general lesson about defaults across three instances in one day, this is the built thing whose repair produced it.

⚠️ AND THE OPPOSITE ERROR IS EQUALLY AVAILABLE: `none` IS AN ANSWER. `auth: none` on an unauthenticated local pipe is a deliberate statement and `ifc:mcp-tools` makes exactly it; sweeping `none` in with `unspecified` would nag a design that had answered honestly.

IT REPORTS, IT DOES NOT JUDGE. Some axes are genuinely meaningless for some boundaries — a library linked into its callers has no endpoint, a one-way feed has no error model a consumer parses. This NAMES which axes are unset and leaves applicability to the design (`dec:report-dont-judge`); a list of required fields would be reflow2 deciding what a mechanical, human or physical interface must look like.

AND IT ASKS IN THE REQUIREMENT'S WORDS, NOT THE COLUMN'S: each unset axis carries its gloss — `payload_schema` reads as "which fields are mandatory, and their types". Pinned by a test, because it is trivially strippable in a refactor and nothing else would notice.

🛑 HONEST LIMIT, ON THE FINDING ITSELF RATHER THAN ONLY IN A COMMENT. `req:interface-spec-complete` names SIX characteristics; the schema has fields for FIVE. There is nowhere to record performance and constraints — rate limits, concurrency, timeouts — so a design can clear this finding completely and still not say what it promises under load. The evidence string says so, because a detector that quietly checks five sixths of a requirement and reports clean is the green-gate-over-what-it-does-not-cover failure.

DISTINCT FROM `cap:a-published-contract-is-asked-for-its-evidence`, built the same day and walking the same published set: that one asks whether anything SHOWS the contract holds, this asks whether the contract is DESCRIBED well enough for anyone to compare it. A design can be in either state alone — a fully specified contract nobody checks, a checked contract nobody described — and one acknowledgement must not settle both. Pinned by a test.
DISTINCT FROM `cap:interface-spec`, which is the WRITE side: `set_interface_spec` and the nine fields. That capability made the axes recordable; this one notices when they were not recorded.
DISTINCT FROM `dec:idea-a-black-box-owes-an-interface-the-way-a-capability-owes-a-requirement`, an OPEN brainstorm where this is idea B. That node's own measurement is now STALE — it recorded 3 of 4 published boundaries incomplete including `ifc:core-api`, which is no longer designated published; the figures above supersede it. Ideas A, C and D there remain unbuilt.

MEASURED ON REFLOW2 ITSELF: of 3 published boundaries, `ifc:graph-export` fires with 6 unset axes; `ifc:mcp-tools-http` fires on `medium` alone; `ifc:mcp-tools` is silent at a genuine 9 of 9.
properties.name: A published contract is asked which of the agreement axes it never filled in
